video-30-days-of-photoshop-cs4y-6ltfo-yo.title: Color Grading in Photoshop: Camera Raw workflow (Day 21 of 30 Days of Photoshop)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-cs4y-6ltfo-yo.summary: This PHLEARN tutorial demonstrates a non-destructive color grading workflow in Photoshop using the Camera Raw filter. The presenter converts the background layer to a smart object, applies a Camera Raw filter as a smart filter, and then uses the Color Grading panel to selectively adjust midtones, shadows, and highlights with Hue/Saturation/Luminance controls. The process emphasizes visual experimentation, a before/after toggle, and blending and balance controls to fine-tune how color grades interact with different tonal ranges. A second sample image is used to show the same workflow in a more romantic, straightforward style. The video also covers re-opening Camera Raw for iterative tweaks and using the filter’s opacity for subtler effects, all within a non-destructive editing setup.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-2wdiiexm7qq-y.title: Remove Distractions in Photoshop - Day 11
video-30-days-of-photoshop-2wdiiexm7qq-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 11 of the 30 Days of Photoshop teaches two primary strategies for removing distractions from images: a rapid, AI-assisted approach using the Remove tool’s Find Distractions option to eliminate wires and other background clutter with a single click, and a painterly approach that combines the Selection Brush Tool with Generative Fill to remove objects by painting over them and letting AI generate clean replacements. The instructor duplicates the background layer for non-destructive editing, demonstrates one-click removal including background elements and people, and then shows how to paint distractions and apply Generative Fill to produce multiple variations (including hair generation where needed). The video also notes manual alternatives such as the Clone Stamp Tool and Spot Healing Brush for those who prefer non-AI workflows. Overall, the lesson emphasizes quick, scalable distraction removal, with a nod to preserving shadows and continuity, and situates these techniques within the broader 30 Days of Photoshop series.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-4ojzs2ligb8-y.title: Using Adobe Camera Raw in Photoshop: Lens Blur, Sky Masking, and a Non-destructive Workflow
video-30-days-of-photoshop-4ojzs2ligb8-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 10 tutorial demonstrates a nondestructive workflow in Photoshop using the integrated Camera Raw tools. The presenter starts by converting the background to a Smart Object, opens Camera Raw to apply Lens Blur for background separation, and then uses Landscape Masking to isolate the sky and push color temperature toward blue. A radial gradient is employed to brighten the subject, followed by targeted color grading on shadows, midtones, and highlights. Throughout, edits are kept nondestructive via Smart Objects and Smart Filters, with the option to reopen Camera Raw at any time to adjust masking or settings. The session emphasizes practical, repeatable steps that beginner-to-intermediate users can adopt directly in their Photoshop workﬂow.”,

video-30-days-of-photoshop-5djl-lr5tgq-y.title: Explore Blending Modes in Photoshop - Day 18 (PHLEARN)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-5djl-lr5tgq-y.summary: In this PHLEARN tutorial, Day 18 of 30 Days of Photoshop systematically demonstrates blending modes and their practical uses. The instructor places blending modes into groups (Normal, Darken, Lighten, Overlay, and the Calculation family) and explains when each group is typically useful. Through a series of non-destructive, hands-on edits, he shows how to composite images, colorize light and color information, and creatively grade with gradient maps. Key techniques include: converting imported images to smart objects for non-destructive edits; using Levels to white out or darken backgrounds in conjunction with Multiply or Screen blend modes; leveraging light leaks and bokeh overlays with Screen or Lighten-based blends; and using gradient maps and Hue/Saturation to color-grade and harmonize a final image. The session emphasizes practical workflow over memorizing every mode, and demonstrates fast iteration with keyboard shortcuts to cycle blending modes.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-6jxr7jkssyy-y.title: Lightroom vs Photoshop Editing – Day 29 (PHLEARN)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-6jxr7jkssyy-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 29 lesson contrasts Lightroom’s batch editing, organization, and cloud-style workflow with Photoshop’s single-image, layer-based editing. The video demonstrates a practical end-to-end workflow: importing a batch of sample images into Lightroom Classic, organizing with catalogs and metadata, rating and filtering to identify favorites, renaming and foldering to mirror the file system, syncing edits across multiple photos, and performing a color-grade pass. It then transitions to Photoshop to perform a sky replacement on a single image, showing layer-based editing, masking, and export of a PSD back into Lightroom. The session emphasizes how Lightroom handles mass photo management and bulk edits while Photoshop handles targeted, composite edits and final fine-tuning.”

video-30-days-of-photoshop-78mcz6bpexm-y.title: PHLEARN: 30 Days of Photoshop 2025 Edition - Intro
video-30-days-of-photoshop-78mcz6bpexm-y.summary: This PHLEARN intro video announces the 2025 edition of 30 Days of Photoshop, hosted by Aaron Nace. It frames the series as rebuilt from the ground up since the 2019 launch, aiming to take learners from opening Photoshop to producing professional images across daily, focused lessons. The host highlights a trajectory from fundamentals to more complex projects, covering both manual techniques and AI-driven tools. Key AI capabilities introduced include generative fill to add or remove content, generative expand to extend image boundaries, and Select Subject for automatic focus on the main subject, alongside dynamic text and retouching and compositing techniques. The video emphasizes a non-destructive workflow using layers and masks, workspace customization, and a deep understanding of color and tone. Viewers are invited to join a newsletter for a printable calendar and a scheduled email series, promising a 30-day mastery by the end of the program.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-7i4uvtykjio-y.title: Composite Lighting with Light Streaks in Photoshop — Day 30 (PHLEARN)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-7i4uvtykjio-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 30 lesson closes the 30 Days of Photoshop series with a final composite project. The instructor imports a subject image and a collection of light-streak assets, then builds a layered, lighting-rich composite using non-destructive workflows: smart objects and smart filters, layer masks, and a variety of blend modes (notably Screen). The process involves masking the subject, duplicating and repositioning light layers, and experimenting with color and exposure through Levels adjustments on RGB channels. A Camera Raw finish (radial gradient, vignette, grain) and a lens blur pass further integrate the lighting with the subject, while techniques like applying images and copying smart filters across layers keep edits flexible. The video emphasizes experimentation and play, with downloadables and a reminder that all steps can be adjusted or undone for different artistic outcomes.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-8hwuwshb9pc-y.title: Day 28: Exporting Images in Photoshop – Layered PSD, JPEG Deliverables, and Camera Raw Tweaks
video-30-days-of-photoshop-8hwuwshb9pc-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 28 walks through practical, non-destructive export workflows in Photoshop. The instructor starts with background editing by replacing city scenery with a nature backdrop using Generative Fill, then removes a logo from the subject’s hat, and groups layers. A smart-filter workflow is shown by combining layers with Apply Image and applying a Camera Raw filter to add a vignette and perform color grading (shadows, midtones, highlights) while maintaining editability. The video emphasizes saving two deliverables: a layered PSD for future edits and a flattened JPEG suitable for print, web, or social sharing. It covers export settings in depth—format choices (PSD vs JPEG vs TIFF/PDF), color space (sRGB with embedded profile), metadata handling, and scale options (1x and 0.5x) to produce multiple sizes from a single project. The result is a clear, repeatable approach to producing web- and print-ready assets from a single Photoshop document.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-a8gwbwmvius-y.title: Dodge & Burn in Photoshop - Day 19 (Non-destructive workflow with adjustment layers, masking, and Blend If)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-a8gwbwmvius-y.summary: This PHLEARN tutorial (Day 19 of 30 Days of Photoshop) surveys both traditional and non-destructive approaches to dodging and burning. It begins by acknowledging the destructive nature of the native Dodge and Burn tools on the background layer, then presents a non-destructive alternative using adjustment layers (notably Brightness/Contrast) with masks that can be toggled, masked, and re-tuned over time. The instructor introduces refining these adjustments with layer masks, inverting masks, and painting with white on the mask; then shows how to isolate edits to the subject using Select Subject and grouping. A highlight is the Blend If technique, which confines dodging/burning to highlights or shadows based on the underlying pixels, enabling very natural results. The video emphasizes a non-destructive, adjustable workflow where edits remain reversible, grouped, and adjustable in real time, and it ends with a downloadable PSD/sample image for hands-on practice.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-dnak4vd6f1u-y.title: Mockup Creation in Photoshop: Three-Phase Workflow with Generative AI, Smart Objects, and Realistic Lighting
video-30-days-of-photoshop-dnak4vd6f1u-y.summary: PHLEARN's Day 26 tutorial demonstrates building a realistic poster mockup in Photoshop through a three-phase workflow. Phase 1 cleans the background by removing unwanted graphics using the Generative AI Remove tool on a new layer, including careful text removal to keep lighting intact. Phase 2 constructs a non-perspective base for the mockup by extracting a billboard’s size with a polygonal Lasso, filling and transforming a white rectangle, then converting it into a Smart Object for non-destructive editing and easy updates. Phase 3 adds realism by duplicating the background into a new layer, applying it as a clipped, soft-light overlay to the mockup, and tweaking with Apply Image, clipping masks, and Levels to replicate shadows and highlights. The session also covers updating inside the smart object in real time, and using Generative Fill to populate the design (e.g., clouds) while maintaining perspective consistency.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-fxohmgrvrza-y.title: Dynamic Text in Photoshop: Auto-Format, Centering, and Masking Behind Objects (Day 14)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-fxohmgrvrza-y.summary: This PHLEARN tutorial (Day 14 of 30 Days of Photoshop) guides viewers through typography basics with the Type tool and the new dynamic text feature. It starts with standard text setup: choosing font, size, weight, alignment, and manual controls for leading and tracking, including mixing bold and regular within a single line and adjusting line breaks. It then introduces dynamic text, demonstrating how converting to dynamic text makes text auto-fit to its bounding box and remain editable, with real-time reflow as the box is resized. Finally, the lesson shows a practical compositing trick: masking the ocean background and unlinking the dynamic text from the mask so the text can sit behind a foreground object (a fish) for a high-end look, with guidance on moving and editing text even after masking.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-gmlizvpir1y-y.title: Color Match in Photoshop - Day 25
video-30-days-of-photoshop-gmlizvpir1y-y.summary: In this PHLEARN Day 25 tutorial, Aaron Nace demonstrates practical methods for color-matching colors from one photo to another in Photoshop. After acknowledging that automatic tools like Match Color and Neural Filters Color Transfer exist, he shows why they can fall short and then teaches a manual, non-destructive workflow centered on a Levels adjustment layer on a smart object. The method includes side-by-side comparison, sampling highlights and shadows with the Eyedropper, and adjusting individual RGB color channels to reproduce the color relationships between images. The video emphasizes iterative tweaking, color theory relationships (opposites for red/cyan, green/magenta, blue/yellow), and straightforward export options for delivering the final result.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-gwjxmna5osm-y.title: Blend If in Photoshop: Sky Replacement and Color Grading (Day 17, PHLEARN)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-gwjxmna5osm-y.summary: PHLEARN's Day 17 in the 30 Days of Photoshop series demonstrates the Blend If feature in Photoshop as a non-destructive method to composite images by controlling visibility with light levels. The video covers basic concepts of Blend If, how to access and interpret the two sliders (current layer and underlying layer), and the use of control points and feathering (via Alt/Option) to create realistic blends. A practical sky replacement workflow illustrates unlinking layer and layer mask, selecting the sky, and adjusting Blend If across both current and underlying layers to harmonize the new sky with the original lighting. The tutorial also explores color grading techniques using a solid color fill layer and a gradient map, showing how Blend If can modulate visibility by color channels, highlights, or shadows. Overall, the video emphasizes non-destructive, adjustable blending for realistic compositing, with before/after comparisons to verify improvements.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-is7ijvctmoa-y.title: Levels vs Curves in Photoshop: Differences, Color Adjustments, and Layer Masks (Day 7)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-is7ijvctmoa-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 7 lesson contrasts Levels and Curves as two core adjustment tools in Photoshop. The video demonstrates how each adjustment controls light and color, beginning with Level’s input/output sliders and black/white/midtone points, then introducing Curves with its multi-point graph and the ability to create midtone shifts and S-curves. It emphasizes the practical equivalence of the two tools for broad edits, while highlighting Curves’ superior control over midtones and individual tonal points. The instructor then explores color adjustments via RGB channels and explains why Color Balance can be more intuitive for global color shifts. A substantial portion covers localized edits using layer masks, gradients, and radial gradients—demonstrating selective lightening of a subject and recoloring the sky with non-destructive workflows. The video concludes with guidance on when to use Levels vs Curves (depending on which interface feels more intuitive) and demonstrates combining both with masks to tune specific parts of an image.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-ja6an971ira-y.title: Correct Exposure in Photoshop - Day 22
video-30-days-of-photoshop-ja6an971ira-y.summary: PHLEARN's Day 22 tutorial demonstrates a non-destructive workflow for correcting image exposure in Photoshop using Adobe Camera Raw. The instructor converts the layer to a smart object via Smart Filters, applies a global Camera Raw auto adjustment, and refines exposure with highlights, shadows, and vibrance. The lesson then masking a subject to apply local adjustments, removes a stray background figure with the Remove tool, automatically straightens the horizon, and revisits Camera Raw to fine-tune skin tones with the Color Mixer (Point Color). The approach emphasizes non-destructive editing with re-editable Camera Raw settings and provides a concise, repeatable sequence for improving exposure while preserving skin tone naturalness.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-jr4plp6iffs-y.title: Change Color in Photoshop – Day 8: Targeted Hue/Saturation Edits and Colorize Techniques
video-30-days-of-photoshop-jr4plp6iffs-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 8 lesson demonstrates how to change the color of objects in Photoshop using a hue/saturation adjustment layer, with emphasis on precise targeting via selection and masking. The tutorial covers selecting the object (a Volkswagen bus) with the Object Selection tool, loading the selection as a layer mask, and using color-based adjustments to alter hue, saturation, and lightness. It shows sampling target colors with the Eyedropper, refining edits with layer masks (painting with black to hide adjustments), and applying multiple Hue/Saturation layers to affect greens, blues, and even a blanket color using the Colorize option. The session concludes with a gradient-based mask for controlled transitions and a reminder to group layers for organization. The workflow is framed as adjustable and non-destructive, enabling quick re-tuning of colors at any time.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-kmdt-znftuk-y.title: Advanced Retouching in Photoshop: Spot Healing, Two‑Pass Blemish Removal, and Frequency Separation (PHLEARN Day 24)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-kmdt-znftuk-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 24 in the 30 Days of Photoshop series demonstrates a two-step, non-destructive approach to advanced retouching: first remove skin blemishes at the pore level using a spot-healing/removal workflow on a dedicated layer, then even out skin tone with a frequency separation action that creates a separate texture layer and a color layer. The tutorial emphasizes preserving skin texture, applying changes at both zoomed-in and zoomed-out scales, and using subtle, painterly blending with sampling via Alt/Option. It covers loading and applying a dedicated frequency separation action (with options for 8-bit JPEGs vs 16-bit RAW), blurring the texture to separate detail from color, organizing edits into a folder, and providing a downloadable PSD for practice. The session also notes the importance of not removing defining features (like moles) and points to a Flur Pro course for deeper learning.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-lgifymd-tze-y.title: PHLEARN 30 Days of Photoshop: Day 1 Tour — Interface, Workspaces, and Core Techniques
video-30-days-of-photoshop-lgifymd-tze-y.summary: This Day 1 tour from PHLEARN’s 30 Days of Photoshop introduces absolute beginners to Photoshop 2025 by outlining the program’s layout, core tools, and how to navigate and customize workspaces. The host demonstrates creating new documents with template options, loading sample assets, and opening images, then moves into hands-on workspace configuration—pinning and saving custom workspaces, switching between built-in layouts, and arranging panels. A practical photo-editing workflow is shown using selection tools, adjustment layers, and non-destructive techniques, followed by tips on preferences, history states, and help resources. The video emphasizes a non-destructive mindset and a tailored, efficient interface to accelerate learning across the 30-day curriculum, with several AI-enabled and modern features highlighted (Generative Crop, Select Subject) for discoverability and searchability.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-llq3mik4gqe-y.title: File formats in Photoshop: PSD/PSB, PDF, TIFF, JPEG/PNG/GIF and exporting workflow
video-30-days-of-photoshop-llq3mik4gqe-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 3 in the 30 Days of Photoshop series demonstrates how to manage and save image files with layers, and to export finalized images for web, print, and social media. The tutorial covers saving layered PSD (and PSB for very large files), PDF and TIFF options for preserving vector data and color depth, and the differences between flattened formats like JPEG and lossless PNG/GIF. It also walks through a practical edit using brightness/contrast adjustments, layer masks with a radial gradient, and a gradient map for color grading, followed by a detailed walkthrough of the Export As dialog to produce web- and print-ready assets at multiple sizes while preserving layer fidelity for future edits.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-lsbtjxx-aco-y.title: Realistic Sky Replacement in Photoshop: Masking, Color Matching, and Light Integration (Day 27)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-lsbtjxx-aco-y.summary: This PHLEARN tutorial (Day 27 of 30 Days of Photoshop) guides learners through replacing a sky in a photograph and making the result look realistic by matching lighting and color. The instructor starts with assessing the original light in the image, selects a warm sky with compatible direction, places the sky into the background, and masks it. He demonstrates unlinking the sky mask to reposition the new sky, flipping the sky to better align light direction, and applying a gradient on a grouped sky to fade it toward the horizon. The core of the workflow centers on color and light harmonization: sampling the original sky color, clipping color balance and levels adjustments to the sky, and tweaking midtones, highlights, and shadows to achieve a natural blend with the foreground. The video emphasizes iterative before/after checks and concludes with tips for final tweaking and the option to download the PSD for study.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-mplf8qaomii-y.title: Cloud-based Select Subject in Photoshop 2025: Subject Brightening, Sunset Glow, and Background Gradient
video-30-days-of-photoshop-mplf8qaomii-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 9 video demonstrates Adobe's cloud-based Select Subject tool in Photoshop 2025 and uses it to separate a subject from the background for targeted edits. The instructor first enables the cloud processing option, then applies Select Subject to create a precise selection that automatically loads into a curves adjustment layer mask, allowing brightness tweaks to the subject via a curves adjustment. A sunset glow is added with a Levels adjustment plus a gradient in the layer mask (radial gradient, with a foreground color chosen and the gradient reversed as needed). In a second example, the subject is again selected, brightness adjusted with brightness/contrast, and the background is enhanced by inverting the selection and painting a gradient glow behind the subject to achieve a more finished look. The video emphasizes the contextual taskbar, cloud-based processing, and the ability to toggle adjustment layers to compare results, and it points viewers to downloadable sample assets to follow along.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-mtqw0jl5m8g-y.title: Understanding Layers in Photoshop - Day 4
video-30-days-of-photoshop-mtqw0jl5m8g-y.summary: PHLEARN's Day 4 core lesson explains why layers are the backbone of non-destructive editing in Photoshop, covering standard layers, adjustment layers, and special layers such as text and shape layers. The video demonstrates building a photo composite by importing a second image as a new layer, adjusting opacity and visibility, and converting a background layer into a regular editable layer. It introduces Smart Objects for nondestructive editing, shows how to create and edit layer masks from selections, and explains the relationship between layers and masks (including unlinking and relinking). The tutorial then guides edge refinement with Select and Mask, the use of clipping masks for effects like light leaks, painting details with brushes to simulate Polaroid edges, and color grading with a gradient map. Finally, it demonstrates applying Gaussian blur and noise to sell realism, all within a fully non-destructive workflow that preserves the original background.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-pgrljpyhzo4-y.title: Layer-based blemish removal, selective redness correction, and eye brightening (Day 23) in Photoshop
video-30-days-of-photoshop-pgrljpyhzo4-y.summary: This PHLEARN tutorial demonstrates non-destructive, layer-based retouching in Photoshop. The instructor walks through starting with blemish removal on a dedicated new layer using the Remove Tool (with Auto mode), then performing targeted color corrections by isolating redness with a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer and an Eyedropper, followed by precise masking to confine edits to skin areas while preserving lips. The workflow proceeds to brighten the eyes with a Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer, using inverted and carefully painted masks to isolate eye regions. The session ends with a quick organizational step—grouping layers—and a quick before/after comparison, plus a note about downloading a PSD to study the edits non-destructively.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-qe0vorgdshy-y.title: Color Correction in Photoshop: Non-destructive Camera Raw Auto and White Balance Eyedropper (PHLEARN Day 20)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-qe0vorgdshy-y.summary: This PHLEARN tutorial demonstrates a fast, non-destructive workflow to color correct photos in Photoshop using the Camera Raw filter. After converting the image to a Smart Object, the host shows color correction techniques applicable to both RAW and JPEG images: using the White Balance Eyedropper to target a neutral gray, discussing the gray-card practice for reliable white balance, and employing the Auto button in Camera Raw for automatic color correction. The instructor emphasizes non-destructive editing by enabling/disabling the smart filter, compares before/after results to illustrate improvements in color and skin tones, and suggests that Auto often performs well across different image formats. The session closes with guidance on when to use these techniques and a tease for the next day's color grading lesson.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-qprdfi8szle-y.title: Liquify Tool in Photoshop: Non-destructive clean-up of clothing edges (Day 15 of 30 Days of Photoshop)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-qprdfi8szle-y.summary: In this PHLEARN tutorial, Aaron Nace demonstrates a practical, non-destructive workflow for using Photoshop's Liquify tool to clean and tighten lines on fashion imagery. The lesson starts with converting the layer to a Smart Object to enable non-destructive edits, then walks through the Forward Warp tool for shaping clothing, the Reconstruct brush as a controlled undo, and the more specialized tools (Pucker, Bloat, Pluck/Blow). A Freeze Mask is introduced to restrict edits, and the session concludes with a strong emphasis on using Generative Fill to remove wrinkles and refine texture, followed by a before/after comparison and guidance on applying these techniques to fashion shoots.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-uuaaj9-lu0a-y.title: Layer Masks in Photoshop - Day 6
video-30-days-of-photoshop-uuaaj9-lu0a-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 6 tutorial demonstrates practical layer-mask techniques for creating a composite in Photoshop. The presenter guides viewers through isolating a subject with a mask, layering background elements (mountains and clouds), using AI Generative Fill to extend the background, and blending the pieces with mask-based adjustments. The video covers refining edges with Select and Mask (including Refine Edge and decontamination of color), adjusting mask density and feathering, unlinking and relinking layer and mask for independent movement, and applying lens blur via Camera Raw on a grouped background. It finishes with adjustment-layer masking (brightness/contrast and gradient maps) to achieve a cohesive, non-destructive final composite, and emphasizes saving as PSD to preserve masks.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-y3sedmqrag0-y.title: Smart Objects in Photoshop - Day 16
video-30-days-of-photoshop-y3sedmqrag0-y.summary: PHLEARN's Day 16 in the 30 Days of Photoshop series explores smart objects and their non-destructive workflow. The tutorial demonstrates how smart objects preserve resolution when scaling, how they differ from rasterized layers, and how they can be edited by opening their contents as a nested document. Aaron Nace walks through building a boxed advertisement: importing images as smart objects, resizing non-destructively, applying non-destructive filters like Gaussian blur, and using masking and dynamic text to composite foreground and background. The video also covers saving the work as a PSD to preserve layers, relinking or replacing smart object contents to update assets, and advanced techniques such as extracting and overlaying reflections with clipping masks and levels for a more realistic result. Throughout, the emphasis is on iterative editing, updating linked assets, and the practical advantages of smart objects in complex composites, with notes on trade-offs like increased file size.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-y8mn2bxh4ps-y.title: Crop, Straighten, and AI-Expand in Photoshop (Day 13) — Composition via Crop Tool
video-30-days-of-photoshop-y8mn2bxh4ps-y.summary: In Day 13 of PHLEARN’s 30 Days of Photoshop, the instructor demonstrates how to crop and straighten an image and then expand the canvas using AI to improve composition. The lesson emphasizes starting with a crooked horizon, choosing and adjusting crop ratios (including square 1:1 and film-like sizes), and using overlays such as rule of thirds and golden spiral to plan placement of subjects. The video contrasts manual straightening via the horizon-drag/rotate approach with the built-in Straighten tool, and shows how to toggle crop shield opacity and reset fixed ratios with the Clear button. A major focus is the Generative Expand AI fill, which can extend the image beyond its original bounds and generate variations in real time to create a more balanced composition. The instructor demonstrates reapplying overlays after AI expansion and iterating between square and other aspect ratios to achieve a final, more intentional crop with improved space around the subjects, guided by compositional rules (rule of thirds, golden spiral) but ultimately flexible to user intent.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-ywswib5ajoe-y.title: Adjustment Layers in Photoshop – Day 5 (PHLEARN)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-ywswib5ajoe-y.summary: PHLEARN’s Day 5 lesson on adjustment layers teaches non-destructive color and light editing in Photoshop. The video defines what adjustment layers are, explains their nondestructive nature and the role of layer masks for selective visibility, and demonstrates how to access and organize these layers via three pathways (Layer menu, layers panel icon, and the Adjustments panel). It then walks through a broad set of adjustment types—starting with a basic Brightness/Contrast example and progressing through Levels, Curves, Exposure, Vibrance, Hue/Saturation, Color Balance, Black & White, Photo Filter, Channel Mixer, Color Lookup (LUTs), and Gradient Map—while illustrating masking techniques, clipping masks, auto-generation, reset, and practical tips for color grading. The session also covers grouping adjustments, saving and re-opening PSDs to preserve edits, and emphasizes using masks and opacity for subtle, non-destructive results.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-yym2sn0ioau-y.title: Open, Edit, and Save in Photoshop (Day 2): Gradient Sun Rays, PSD Workflow, and JPEG Export
video-30-days-of-photoshop-yym2sn0ioau-y.summary: PHLEARN's Day 2 Photoshop tutorial demonstrates a practical workflow for opening various image files, editing with layered gradients to simulate sunlight, and saving and exporting in multiple formats. The instructor walks through opening images via drag-and-drop, the Open dialog, keyboard shortcuts, and recent files; builds a gradient sun effect with a radial gradient on a dedicated layer using the Screen blend mode; samples sky colors with the Eyedropper; creates light rays with a brush on a new layer, applies a radial blur, duplicates and merges layers, then transforms and refines the result with a layer mask. The session emphasizes keeping a layered PSD for future edits and producing a compressed JPEG for sharing, including sRGB conversion and quality settings. The video also contrasts PSD retention with export workflows and previews the topic of file formats in the next lesson.

video-30-days-of-photoshop-zm5irojxdty-y.title: Photoshop: Non-destructive Scale, Rotate & Align with Smart Objects and Alignment Tools (Day 12)
video-30-days-of-photoshop-zm5irojxdty-y.summary: This 30 Days of Photoshop tutorial demonstrates a non-destructive workflow for scaling, rotating, and aligning layers. It starts with placing a stock image into a background frame as a Smart Object, then explores transform options (center vs corner pivot, alt/option-centered scaling, width/height linking), and uses keyboard modifiers to skew, perspective, and rotate. The lesson then shows masking a frame and adding an inner shadow for depth, followed by extracting a signature from a JPEG, converting it to a Smart Object, and using color range and fills to shape the result. The core focus culminates in alignment techniques: aligning multiple layers and aligning within selections using Photoshop’s Move tool and alignment controls, including converting layer masks to selections for precise placement. All steps illustrate a non-destructive approach with easily toggled visibility and editable transforms.
